passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: This Management’s Discussion and Analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes that appear elsewhere in this Annual Report. In addition to historical information, the following discussion contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ substantially and adversely from those referred to herein due to a number of factors, including but not limited to those described below and in “ Item 1A - Risk Factors” and elsewhere in this Annual Report. The following section generally discusses our financial condition and results of operations for our fiscal year ended October 3, 2025 (“fiscal year 2025 ”) compared to our fiscal year ended September 27, 2024 (“fiscal year 2024”). A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal year 2024 compared to our fiscal year ended September 29, 2023 (“fiscal year 2023”) can be found in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on November 12, 2024. OVERVIEW We design and manufacture semiconductor products and solutions for I&D, Data Center and Telecom industries. Headquartered in Lowell, Massachusetts, we have more than 70 years of application expertise, with silicon, GaAs, GaN and InP fabrication, manufacturing, assembly and test, and operational facilities throughout North America, Europe and Asia. We design, develop and manufacture differentiated semiconductor products and solutions for customers who demand high performance, quality and reliability. We offer a broad portfolio of thousands of standard and custom devices, which include ICs, MCMs, diodes, amplifiers, switches and switch limiters, passive and active components and RF and optical subsystems, which make up dozens of product lines that service over 6,000 end customers in our three primary markets. Our semiconductor products are electronic components that our customers generally incorporate into larger electronic systems, such as wireless basestations, high-capacity optical networks, data center networks, radar, medical systems, satellite networks and test and measurement applications. Our primary end markets are: (1) I&D, which includes military and commercial radar, RF jammers, electronic countermeasures, communication data links, space-related electronics and various wired and wireless multi-market applications, which include industrial, medical, test and measurement and scientific applications; (2) Data Center, which includes intra-Data Center, DCI applications, at 100G, 200G, 400G, 800G, 1.6T, 3.2T and higher speeds, enabled by our broad portfolio of analog ICs and photonic components for high speed connectivity customers; and (3) Telecom, which includes carrier infrastructure such as long-haul/metro, 5G and 6G infrastructure, SATCOM and FTTx/PON, among others. See “ Item 1 - Business ” for additional information. 29 Basis of Presentation We have one reportable operating segment and all intercompany balances have been eliminated in consolidation. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following risks and other information in this Annual Report in evaluating the Company and its common stock. If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition or results of operations could suffer. The risks described below are not the only ones facing us. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial may also adversely affect our Company. Risks Relating to General Business Conditions We operate in the semiconductor industry, which is cyclical and subject to significant downturns. The semiconductor industry is highly cyclical and is characterized by constant and rapid technological change, price erosion, product obsolescence, evolving standards, short product lifecycles and significant fluctuations in supply and demand. The industry has historically experienced significant fluctuations in demand and product obsolescence, resulting in product overcapacity, high inventory levels and accelerated erosion of average selling prices (“ASPs”). For instance, the capital spending on Data Center infrastructure to support artificial intelligence (“AI”) applications is rapidly expanding, which is increasing demand for our products. If capital spending on Data Center infrastructure slows down, demand for our products may decline. Downturns in our industry may be prolonged, and downturns in many sectors of the electronic systems industry have in the past contributed to extended periods of weak demand for semiconductor products. We have experienced decreases in our revenue, profitability, cash flows and stock price during such downturns in the past, and may be similarly harmed by future downturns, particularly if we are unable to effectively respond to reduced demand in a particular market. Our revenue growth and gross margin are substantially dependent on our successful development and release of new products. Maintaining or growing our revenue will depend, among other things, on our ability to timely develop products for existing and new markets that meet customers’ performance, reliability and price expectations. In addition, the ASPs of our products may decrease over time, and we must introduce new products that can be manufactured at lower costs or that command higher prices based on superior performance to offset price erosion. If we are not able to introduce products that ship in volume, our revenue will likely not grow and may decline significantly and rapidly. The development of products in our industry is a highly complex process, and we have in the past, and may in the future, experience delays and failures in completing the development and introduction of new products. credit_strengths.text: Revenue and operating income both expanded year over year, with the operating margin holding near the low teens and comfortably above the prior-year level. Growth is broad-based across the issuer's three end markets, and the Data Center buildout for AI infrastructure is a visible demand driver. This scale supports the fixed-cost absorption underpinning the current earnings base.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure several times over, leaving substantial free cash flow after the modest capex program. Cash generation is the primary source of liquidity and comfortably funds the disclosed buyback and small bolt-on acquisition spend. This internally funded model limits reliance on external financing for routine investment.

key_risks.text: The issuer operates in a highly cyclical semiconductor industry marked by rapid technological change, price erosion and product obsolescence. Management explicitly warns that AI-driven Data Center capital spending could slow, weakening demand, and that revenue growth depends on timely new product releases. Past downturns have reduced revenue, profitability and cash flow, and similar pressure could recur.

Debt is entirely long-term borrowings split between current maturities and noncurrent balances, with no separately tagged short-term borrowings or commercial paper. The disclosed maturity schedule is empty, so the refinancing profile cannot be assessed from the bundle. This is a material data gap for judging rollover risk, though the net cash position and strong coverage mitigate near-term concern.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income many times the reported interest expense, and free cash flow to debt is healthy. The issuer holds a net cash position once cash and short-term investments are measured against debt, and the indicative financial risk profile is minimal. This headroom comfortably absorbs moderate earnings volatility.

Liquidity is robust: the current ratio is well above the sector median, and cash plus internally generated funds cover the modest capex, buyback and acquisition uses. The debt stack carries no tagged short-term borrowings, so refinancing needs appear limited. We view debt service as comfortably manageable absent a severe, prolonged industry downturn.

overall_credit_view.text: We view the credit profile as strong, supported by expanding revenue, solid operating margins, minimal net leverage and very high interest coverage. Free cash flow after capex is substantial and funds shareholder returns and small acquisitions. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, and the Altman Z double-prime zone is safe, reinforcing a favorable assessment.

The principal credit sensitivities are semiconductor cyclicality, dependence on AI-related Data Center spending and new product execution, plus the absence of a disclosed maturity schedule. We would monitor demand trends and the debt maturity profile as the key forward-looking variables. On balance, we expect the issuer to sustain comfortable debt service through the cycle.

credit_strengths.text: 收入及經營溢利均按年擴張，經營利潤率維持於低雙位數附近，並穩固地高於去年同期水平。增長在發行人的三個終端市場中廣泛呈現，而為 AI 基礎設施而設的數據中心建設是可見的需求驅動因素。此規模支持固定成本吸收，支撐當前盈利基礎。
經營現金流覆蓋資本開支數倍以上，在溫和的資本開支計劃後留下大量自由現金流。現金產生是流動性的主要來源，並從容地為已披露的回購及小型補強式收購支出提供資金。此內部融資模式限制了對外部融資的依賴以進行日常投資。

key_risks.text: 發行人經營於高度週期性的半導體行業，其特徵為技術快速變化、價格侵蝕及產品過時。管理層明確警告，AI 驅動的數據中心資本開支可能放緩，削弱需求，且收入增長取決於及時推出新產品。過往的低迷期曾減少收入、盈利能力及現金流，類似壓力可能重現。
債務全為長期借款，分為流動到期部分及非流動結餘，並無單獨標示的短期借款或商業票據。已披露的到期時間表為空白，因此無法從資料包中評估再融資狀況。這是判斷展期風險的重大數據缺口，儘管淨現金狀況及強勁覆蓋率緩解了近期憂慮。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，經營溢利為報告利息開支的許多倍，而自由現金流對債務比率亦健康。一旦以現金及短期投資與債務作衡量，發行人持有淨現金狀況，而指示性財務風險狀況為極低。此緩衝從容地吸收適度的盈利波動。
流動性穩健：流動比率遠高於行業中位數，而現金加上內部產生的資金覆蓋溫和的資本開支、回購及收購用途。債務結構並無標示的短期借款，因此再融資需求似乎有限。我們認為，在沒有嚴重且持久的行業低迷下，債務償付從容可控。

overall_credit_view.text: 我們認為信貸狀況強勁，受到收入擴張、穩健經營利潤率、極低淨槓桿及極高利息覆蓋率支持。資本開支後的自由現金流可觀，並為股東回報及小型收購提供資金。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，而 Altman Z 雙素區間為安全，強化了有利評估。
主要信貸敏感因素為半導體週期性、對 AI 相關數據中心開支的依賴及新產品執行，加上缺乏已披露的到期時間表。我們將監測需求趨勢及債務到期狀況作為關鍵前瞻性變數。總體而言，我們預期發行人可在週期中維持從容的債務償付。
